text:
**I’d pick Starling if you’re a UK sole trader or small limited company mainly paid by bank transfer.** There’s no monthly fee, standard UK bank transfers are free, and you can create and send invoices without paying for an upgrade. You can also set money aside for tax and connect Xero, QuickBooks or FreeAgent. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/sole-trader-bank-account/?utm_source=openai))

I’d change that recommendation in three cases:

| If you… | I’d choose | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Want bookkeeping software included** | **Mettle** | FreeAgent is included if you make at least **one transaction a month** from the account. That can save you a separate subscription. Mettle accepts eligible sole traders and limited companies with up to two owners. ([mettle.co.uk](https://www.mettle.co.uk/business-bank-account/)) |
| **Regularly pay in modest amounts of cash** | **Monzo Business Lite** | Cash deposits cost **£1 each** at a Post Office or PayPoint, versus **0.7%, minimum £3**, at a Post Office with Starling. Check the monthly Monzo cap: **£3,000 for sole traders** or **£10,000 for limited companies**. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/business-accounts/how-to-cash-deposit-business-account-web?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Want a branch or expect to apply for lending** | **HSBC Small Business Banking Account** | There’s no monthly fee, standard UK digital transfers are free, and you can apply for lending. Branch transactions can cost extra, so check the tariff for anything you’ll do regularly. ([business.hsbc.uk](https://www.business.hsbc.uk/en-gb/products/small-business-bank-account?cid=HBUK%3AAT%3ASBBA%3AP1%3ACMB%3AL8%3AGO+%3APRP%3A0%3ACA%3A13%3A0225%3A001%3ABingPPCBrand&utm_source=openai)) |

For a freelancer invoicing UK clients, the deciding question is **whether you’d otherwise pay for FreeAgent**. If yes, I’d go with **Mettle**; if you just want to invoice clients, get paid and put tax money aside, I’d go with **Starling**. ([mettle.co.uk](https://www.mettle.co.uk/business-bank-account/))
